- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  Mother with severe migraines (with vomiting). No other family history recorded.  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  Combined oral contraceptive pill (exact product not documented) — dose/route/frequency not documented; Ibuprofen as needed for headache — dose/route/frequency not documented; New NSAID prescribed (name not documented) — dose/route/frequency not documented; Acetaminophen (paracetamol) advised to take with NSAID — dose/route/frequency not documented.

- Summary and reasoning: New-onset, severe, continuous headache for 3 days with photophobia and positive visual phenomena (“shooting lights”), right supraorbital predominance, mild nausea, partial response to NSAID, no focal neurologic deficits, afebrile by history. Family history positive for migraine (mother). On estrogen-containing combined oral contraceptive.  
- Working diagnosis: Migraine with aura, possible status migrainosus — supported by migrainous features (photophobia, visual phenomena, nausea), unilateral emphasis, family history, and persistent symptoms.  
- DDx considerations (from DDx, consistent with transcript):
  - Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) — Medium likelihood: new severe headache in a woman on estrogen OCP; visual symptoms; some positional sensitivity; no focal deficits reported.
  - Tension-type headache — Low–Medium likelihood: continuous bilateral pressure possible, but severity and migrainous features reduce likelihood.  
- Conflict noted: None between transcript and DDx.

  - Prescribed a stronger NSAID (name not documented); advised concurrent acetaminophen and to take with food.
  - Advised to book an in-person clinic appointment for full neurologic examination, fundoscopic exam (“look at the back of the eyes”), and blood pressure check.
  - Safety net: If headache worsens, becomes unbearable, or changes character, attend emergency department (A&E).
  - OCP counseling: If migraine with aura is confirmed, the current combined OCP may be unsuitable and would need review/change.
